senses.sense_definition: A smooth tool used to help slide the heel into a shoe.

examples.text: He used a <w>shoehorn</w> to put on his tight leather boots.
My grandfather always keeps a <w>shoehorn</w> by the front door.

senses.sense_definition: Something that helps to facilitate or start a process or transaction.

examples.text: The new policy acted as a <w>shoehorn</w> for the difficult merger negotiations.
They used the small grant as a <w>shoehorn</w> to secure larger investments.

senses.sense_definition: A person or thing that acts as an inducement or lure.

examples.text: He was merely a <w>shoehorn</w> used to attract more wealthy guests to the party.
The company used the celebrity as a <w>shoehorn</w> to gain public interest.

traits.comment: Used in a historical context to describe social manipulation.

senses.sense_definition: To force something into a tight space or a busy schedule.

examples.text: We had to <w>shoehorn</w> all our luggage into the small trunk.
The assistant tried to <w>shoehorn</w> another meeting into his busy afternoon.

senses.sense_definition: To force an event to fit into an unrelated agenda or theory.

examples.text: Critics argued that the author tried to <w>shoehorn</w> his political views into the story.
It is common for conspiracy theorists to <w>shoehorn</w> random events into their false narratives.

senses.sense_definition: To use a shoehorn to put on footwear.

examples.text: You should <w>shoehorn</w> your boots to avoid damaging the back of the leather.
He <w>shoehorned</w> his feet into the new shoes before leaving the house.
